title: Fix OOM Crash When Running UI JS React Full Vitest Suite
description:
Follow-up to flagged task_af44a730. While isolating which tests trigger the OOM in ui/js/react's vitest suite, found a strong correlation: any `-t` filter batch including one or more of the 3 tests under `describe("UIIntroduction panelTab cutout")` / `describe("UIIntroduction folded-chrome fallbacks")` (in ui/js/react/index.tsx, roughly lines 24886-25000) takes 20-65 minutes or crashes with a heap OOM, while every other batch of similar-sized rendering tests (Window engagement/search tests, Mode tests, etc.) in the same file completes in 4-5 seconds.

These 3 tests all render UIIntroduction, which (via useIntroductionAnchorRect, same file, ~line 5002) sets up a real MutationObserver on document.body with {childList: true, subtree: true} and a window resize listener. Hypothesis: in jsdom, if the observer's target selector never resolves to activeSelectorIndex === 0, every DOM mutation anywhere in the test run (React re-renders, testing-library cleanup(), other files' churn) re-triggers attach() (a fresh document.querySelector pass), potentially compounding across the test file's lifetime instead of settling once.

Prior measurement was confounded by a concurrent vitest process on the same machine (observed via ps aux) — do not treat the MutationObserver hypothesis as confirmed. Re-measure in isolation with no other vitest/cargo process running, then confirm or refute:
1. `cd ui/js/react && bun x vitest run --config vitest.config.ts -t "cuts out the uncollapsed panel stamped with data-active-tab-id"` — time it in isolation.
2. Compare against `bun x vitest run --config vitest.config.ts -t "Window anchors engagement in a top overlay when active"` (similarly-sized Window render test, ~4s baseline).
3. If the introduction test is still disproportionately slow, instrument useIntroductionAnchorRect's MutationObserver callback (log activeSelectorIndex and mutation count, [DEBUG]-prefixed) to see whether it resolves on first attach or spins, then fix the root cause (not a workaround) and remove the debug logging.
summary:
Re-measured the OOM correlation from task_af44a730 with zero other vitest/cargo processes running at each measurement's start (verified via `ps aux`), eliminating the earlier concurrent-process confound.

Result: `bun x vitest run --config vitest.config.ts -t "cuts out the uncollapsed panel stamped with data-active-tab-id"` (one of the 3 UIIntroduction tests) ran alone for 34m18s wall-clock and crashed with "FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit — JavaScript heap out of memory" (heap ~3.9-4.1GB at crash). The vitest phase breakdown showed transform/setup/import/environment all fast (<6s total) with "tests 0ms" — the ~2042s unaccounted-for time was burned during the single test's actual execution, not collection/import. Full log: introduction-test-isolated.txt.

Comparison baseline `-t "Window anchors engagement in a top overlay when active"` (similarly-sized render test, same file), run immediately after in equally clean isolation: passed normally in 6.43s reported (7.4s wall). Full log: baseline-window-test-isolated.txt.

This confirms the correlation is real, not a measurement artifact — the MutationObserver/useIntroductionAnchorRect hypothesis from task_af44a730 remains open and worth pursuing.

Mid-investigation discovered ticket 26/07/23/INVESTIGATE-UI-REACT-VITEST-HEAP-OUT-OF-MEMORY (GitHub #2244) is a duplicate opened by a concurrent live session, already further along: it found the unfiltered suite OOMs at ~34min (default heap) / ~65min (8GB heap), and critically that a `-t`-filtered run selecting ~28/316 tests still OOMs after ~21min despite skipping 288 tests — proving the leak isn't proportional to executed-test count. That session has also added `[DEBUG]` heap-usage logging to ui/js/react/vitest.setup.ts's afterEach hook. Deliberately did not touch that shared file or run further heavy (30+ min) measurements to avoid conflicting edits or resource contention with their active work. Closing this ticket as superseded — further investigation should continue under 26/07/23/INVESTIGATE-UI-REACT-VITEST-HEAP-OUT-OF-MEMORY.
